events.title: Kotlin made official for Android
events.summary: At Google I/O on May 17, 2017, Google announced Kotlin as an officially supported language for Android development alongside Java.
events.about: Google's endorsement turned Kotlin from a JetBrains side project into the default choice for new Android apps. Null safety, coroutines, and Java interop let teams migrate gradually off verbose Android Java without rewriting entire codebases overnight.

narrative.whyChosen: Google's backing made Kotlin the successor to Java on the world's largest mobile platform.
narrative.whyImportant: Millions of Android developers gained a modern language with first-class IDE and docs support.
narrative.problemSolved: Android Java was verbose and null-prone; Google needed an official modern alternative developers would adopt.

sources.title: Google I/O 2017 — Kotlin on Android announcement (May 17, 2017)

events.title: Node.js 8 released
events.summary: Node.js 8.0.0 shipped on May 30, 2017 with V8 5.8, async/await enabled by default, and npm 5.
events.about: Node 8 became LTS in October 2017 — bringing native `async`/`await` to server JavaScript without transpilers. npm 5 added package-lock.json by default, stabilizing dependency trees for millions of projects.

narrative.whyChosen: Node 8 made async/await the standard pattern for Node.js servers.
narrative.whyImportant: Native async syntax eliminated callback pyramids in production codebases.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams transpiled async/await or chained Promises manually before Node 8.
